stem.text: Light of wavelength $\lambda$ is emitted from two point sources R and S and falls onto a distant screen.

stem.alt: Diagram with point sources R and S on the left and a screen on the right, with point P marked on the screen. The note NOT TO SCALE is shown.

stem.text: At point P on the screen, the light intensity is zero.
What could explain the zero intensity at P?

A.text: Light from the two sources is emitted $180^{\circ}$ out of phase and the path difference to P is $\dfrac{1}{2}\lambda$.

B.text: Light from the two sources is emitted in phase and the path difference to P is $\lambda$.

C.text: Light from the two sources is emitted $90^{\circ}$ out of phase and the path difference to P is $\lambda$.

D.text: Light from the two sources is emitted in phase and the path difference to P is $\dfrac{1}{2}\lambda$.
